chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Sa'd ibn Taref, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
Whoever washes a deceased person and fulfills the trust regarding him, Allah will forgive him. I said, 'And how does he fulfill the trust regarding him?' He said, 'He does not narrate what he sees.'

key_terms.الْأَمَانَة: The trust or confidentiality owed to the deceased during ritual washing

ai.seo_question: How is the 'trust' defined when washing a deceased person in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), emphasizing that the 'trust' (amanah) in washing a deceased believer is primarily maintained through modesty and discretion. By refraining from pointing out or narrating physical defects observed during the ritual, the washer preserves the dignity of the deceased, a key virtue in Shia fiqh. This act of quiet reverence transforms a physical duty into a spiritual merit, securing divine forgiveness for the performer.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Sa’ad Bin Tareyf, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The one who washes a deceased and fulfills the entrustments with regards to him, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Forgive him’. I said, ‘And would he fulfill the entrustments with regards to him?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He would not narrate with what he saw’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Um ay r from Sa‘d ibn Tarif who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said,
Tf one washes a dead body and keeps the trust, Allah grants him forgiveness.’ He was asked, ‘What is the trust?’ The Imam replied, ‘Does not make public whatever he sees.’”
